{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Gail Susan Nelson''' (born 1959){{r|born}} is a mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at [[Carleton College]].{{r|carleton}}

==Education and career==
Nelson did her undergraduate studies at the [[University of North Dakota]].{{r|carleton}}
She completed her Ph.D. in 1988 at the [[University of Minnesota]]. Her dissertation concerned [[partial differential equation]]s, and was supervised by Eugene Barry Fabes; it was ''Bounds for the Fundamental Solutions of Degenerate Parabolic Partial Differential Equations''.{{r|mgp}}
She joined the Carleton College faculty in the same year.{{r|carleton}}

==Books==
Nelson is the author of two textbooks in mathematics:
*''Recurrence and Topology'' (with John M. Alongi, [[Graduate Studies in Mathematics]] 85, American Mathematical Society, 2007), on [[dynamical system]]s.{{r|rat}}
*''A User-Friendly Introduction to Lebesgue Measure and Integration'' (Student Mathematical Library 78, American Mathematical Society, 2015), on [[Lebesgue integration]].{{r|ufi}}
She is also the editor-in-chief of the "Problem Books" book series of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].{{r|maaseries}}
